title: Contextual telemetry sampler for multi-tier region & fallback routing decisions
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: routing decision logs for region selection, tier routing, and fallback model variants are high-volume and noisy — we cannot retain full per-request traces at scale without prohibitive storage and query costs. Goal: introduce a contextual telemetry sampler that keeps high-signal routing traces (per-hop micrometrics, policy rationale, fallback snapshots) while aggressively reducing low-value volume. The sampler should be adaptive (signal-driven), configurable per-project/tier, and able to attach compact provenance IDs and links to full snapshots on-demand.

Scope and deliverables:
- Sampling policy engine: rules evaluate signals (latency percentiles, error rates, model variant mismatch, cost delta, customer tier, region mismatch, circuit-breaker events) to decide full-trace, partial-trace, or metadata-only retention.
- Per-hop micrometrics: capture compact metrics for each routing hop (decision latency, queue time, selected tier, chosen model variant id, fallback reason) with an option to include KV cache hit/miss and batch size.
- Snapshot capture: when sampling triggers full retention, attach compressed snapshot containing prompt prefix (redacted), model variant config, routing policy version, trace id, and references to request/response artifacts.
- Adaptive backpressure: if storage ingestion lags, automatically increase sampling thresholds and emit telemetry about dropped-trace rates.
- Queryability: expose retained traces in Console (routing inspector) with quick filters (region, tier, fallback-reason, request-latency-bucket).
- Config: per-customer and global defaults; toggles for GDPR redaction and PII stripping; retention policies per class (full vs. summary).
- Observability integrations: attach provenance_id to traces so logs/metrics/alerts can correlate; link to existing trace store and tracing UI.

Design trade-offs considered:
- Sampling granularity vs. diagnosis fidelity: we favor keeping full traces for outliers and policy drift events, and summaries for steady-state traffic.
- Retention cost vs. incident readiness: allow short-term higher-fidelity windows (e.g., 72h) that roll down to compact summaries to limit long-term storage cost.
- Privacy: default redaction of request payloads and designer-review gating for any opt-in full-capture.

Instrumentation plan:
1) Lightweight release that emits per-decision metadata (provenance_id, hop_index, selected_tier, selected_model_id, decision_ms, queue_ms, cache_hit) for 100% requests (summary mode).
2) Sampling engine rollout behind feature flag; initial policy: full-trace on 0.1% deterministic sampling + triggers for latency > p99, error_count > 3 in 1m, any cross-region fallback, or canary rollout mismatches.
3) Storage path: compressed snapshots to object store with manifest entries in our telemetry index; trace index stores compact summary records for fast queries.
4) Console work: routing inspector filter and link to snapshot viewer (UX ticket in product-management).

Success metrics:
- 90% reduction in stored trace volume vs. naive full-trace retention for a typical workload sample.
- Time to root-cause for routing incidents <= current baseline (no regression).
- Ability to surface top-5 fallback reasons and region mismatch hotspots within Console.

Risks and mitigations:
- Missed signals due to overly aggressive sampling: mitigation = conservative default thresholds + emergency snapshot mode tied to alert rules.
- Storage ingestion bottleneck during incidents: mitigation = adaptive backpressure + circuit-breaker that falls back to summary-mode and emits metrics.
- Compliance: ensure redaction hooks and customer-controlled toggles; involve Security for review.

Deliverables and milestones:
- Prototype: sampling engine + summary emitter (Week 1-2)
- Beta: snapshot storage + Console links + basic policies (Week 3-5)
- GA: per-tenant config, retention controls, adaptive backpressure (Week 6-8)
